verdict.rationale: No first-party evidence shows Kimi publishing its source code (for example the Kimi Code CLI or the assistant app) under a named open license, or links to any public repository. The only openness signals are community comments calling the K3 model 'open-weight' and 'open source'. Those name no license or readable source and are not vendor documentation, so they cannot establish the capability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
